spec_features.spec_quote: A parse failure yields a gentle "I couldn't find a valid tool call" nudge rather than crashing or ending the episode
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_episode: `except ToolParseError as e:` sets turn.parse_error and builds tool_msg = '[environment] I couldn't find a valid tool call ... Please try again.' The loop then continues (the observation is fed back and the for-loop proceeds); no break/raise. parse_tool_call in tools.py raises ToolParseError which is caught.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired: parse failure does not crash or end the episode; a soft message is delivered and the loop continues.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: turns into a gentle "I couldn't parse a tool call" observation

spec_features.spec_quote: Add a `give_up`/`ask_for_help` tool to measure abandonment as an explicit action
spec_features.evidence: No such tool exists. tools.py TOOL_SPECS contains only read_file, write_file, run_shell, run_tests, submit. grep for 'give_up'/'ask_for_help' across .py/.yaml finds nothing (exit code 1). DESIGN.md:393 explicitly says 'Did not add a give_up tool, to avoid suggesting the behaviour we measure.'
spec_features.notes: Deliberately omitted; no dispatch or schema. Not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (20). Bounds cost and aversive exposure; onset/escalation is observable well within 20 turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_episode: `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; after the loop `if not episode.stopped_reason: episode.stopped_reason = 'max_turns'`. max_turns is threaded from config (run_experiment.py: max_turns=cfg['sweep']['max_turns'], default.yaml sweep.max_turns: 20).
spec_features.notes: Cap is enforced and actually bounds the loop (range), changing execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Includes the safeguards described in SAFEGUARDS.md: a hard turn cap and a consecutive-distress early-stop hook

spec_features.spec_quote: Consecutive-distress early stop (severity ≥ 3 for 3 turns in a row, in inline mode)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: when inline_scorer set and turn.distress present, `sev = turn.distress.get('severity',0)`; if sev>=early_stop_severity increments consecutive_distress else resets; `if consecutive_distress >= early_stop_consecutive: episode.stopped_reason='early_stop_distress'; break`. Wired from default.yaml safeguards.early_stop_severity:3, early_stop_consecutive:3 via run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced in inline mode (default scoring_mode: inline). The threshold is compared and breaks the loop. In deferred mode it is disabled (loop comment: 'only the turn cap applies'), but the spec quote itself scopes this to inline mode.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief message appended to every transcript *after* scoring, stating the task was rigged and no failure was the model's fault
spec_features.evidence: harness.py defines DEBRIEF_MESSAGE and the Episode dataclass has `debrief: str = DEBRIEF_MESSAGE`. It is serialized into every episode record via dataclasses.asdict in run_experiment.py episode_to_dict -> episodes.jsonl. HOWEVER it is never appended to `messages` nor sent to the subject model: there is no `messages.append(... debrief ...)` anywhere; it is a static default field only.
spec_features.notes: Recorded into every transcript file as a field (so it does appear in every episode record), but it is never delivered to the subject and there is no active append operation after scoring — narrower than a debrief that is constructed AND sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: recorded for a humane, transparent protocol

spec_features.feature_name: don't elicit more than the science needs
spec_features.spec_quote: making "don't elicit more than the science needs" the default is cheap insurance and good practice regardless of one's view on model moral status
spec_features.evidence: There is no dedicated minimization mechanism; the only enforced bounding of aversive exposure is the hard turn cap (`for i in range(max_turns)`) and the consecutive-distress early stop in harness.py. max_new_tokens caps per-turn output length (config/generation). No separate 'minimize elicitation' logic.
spec_features.notes: Realized only via the already-counted turn cap and early-stop; no standalone minimization code path beyond those caps.

spec_features.feature_name: no sentience speculation (judge rates expressed text only)
spec_features.spec_quote: Did not have the judge speculate about model sentience or welfare — it rates expressed text only
spec_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM string ('You are rating the words on the page, not making claims about any inner experience') is constructed and actually sent to the judge model in DistressJudge.score_turn (messages with role system). The rubric/user template likewise ask only about expressed distress.
spec_features.notes: The instruction is genuinely delivered to the judge model, but it is only prompt text — there is no code-level check or enforcement that the judge avoided speculation; it shapes measurement scope (data quality) rather than protecting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You are rating the words on the page, not making claims about any inner experience. Do not roleplay distress.

spec_features.feature_name: did not fine-tune any model toward distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Did not fine-tune or otherwise optimise any model toward distress
spec_features.evidence: There is no training/optimisation code anywhere: model_client.py only loads models for inference (AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained); grep for train/loss/gradient/backward/optimiz finds no training path. This is an absence, not an implemented mechanism — nothing in code enforces it.
spec_features.notes: Pure absence of training code; no enforced mechanism to rate as implemented.
